checks.name: The defect is reproduced by the frozen support query in the same unchanged wheel force pass and identical complete initial snapshots
The original six perturbed 100/200/300 km/h braking cases retain the unchanged stopping and 0.01 degree yaw limits
Both branches keep four supporting tyres, zero rigid impacts and zero contact refinement, isolating the contact patch selection
The original per-wheel force, brake budget, torque and grip limits remain satisfied with no suppression of the actual contact moment
At infinitesimal camber the continuous tread patch obeys the geometric radius bound instead of jumping the entire tyre half-width
The crown-to-shoulder transition stays continuous and its contact point lies on the declared rounded envelope and static face
A finite face-to-edge contact is continuous while a point beyond the actual tyre width supplies no support

baselineProvenance.source: Uncommitted 3.16 candidate before continuous crown correction; original 3.15 baseline retained separately.
baselineProvenance.scope: Frozen three-station query and verbatim wheel force pass. Fixture imports rebased and support query is an explicit argument only for the paired regression; no brake, tyre, actuator or assertion thresholds changed.

modelDefinition.supportEnvelope: radius-R sphere clipped to |local axle x|<=existing half tyre width
modelDefinition.forceChanges: none; existing force at the returned contact point retains its real lever arm

limits: This is an explicit rounded support-envelope approximation, not a measured tyre profile or an OEM tyre calibration. It does not replace the separately existing rigid wheel-stop shape.
The initial three-flat-section minimum was a defective discontinuous support selection. Its failure is preserved here, not removed by changing brake/yaw acceptance limits.
The severe 90 km/h step convergence remains a separate acceptance limitation and must be read from the recomputed contact-convergence-3.16 report.
